question: Your customer support agent checks return eligibility before it calls process_refund. The lookup_order tool returns delivery dates as Unix timestamps and order status as numeric codes, while the get_customer tool returns dates as ISO 8601 strings. The agent sometimes misreads the timestamps and approves returns outside the 30-day return window. Which change most reliably makes the agent work with one consistent data format?

options.text: Add few-shot examples to the system prompt that show the agent how to convert Unix timestamps and numeric status codes before it checks the return window.
options.reason: Prompt-based guidance gives only probabilistic compliance, so the agent can still misread a timestamp; a hook gives a deterministic transformation.

options.text: Implement a PostToolUse hook that converts the lookup_order timestamps and status codes into ISO 8601 dates and readable labels before the agent processes them.
options.reason: A PostToolUse hook intercepts tool results and normalizes heterogeneous formats before the model processes them, so the agent always sees one format.

options.text: Add a custom convert_formats MCP tool and instruct the agent in the system prompt to call it on every lookup_order result before it decides whether the order is still inside the return window.
options.reason: The conversion still depends on the agent choosing to follow a prompt instruction, which is probabilistic rather than a guaranteed normalization of tool results.

options.text: Route every return request to the escalate_to_human tool so that a human reviewer checks the order dates and status codes before any refund is processed.
options.reason: This avoids the format problem instead of normalizing the data, and escalating every return works against the 80%+ first-contact resolution target.
